description: This skill group explains how to review Form.io JSON files for unsafe calculated display values, JavaScript runtime errors or Form.io console warnings, and forbidden debug logging statements inside executable logic.
goal: Review a Form.io JSON file and determine PASSED or FAILED for each check, with exact failure locations, reasons, and safer recommendations when a rule is violated.

rules: For every check, return PASSED or FAILED.
Do not assume a pass when evidence is missing.
If one item breaks the rule, that check must be FAILED.
If failed, clearly point out the exact component, logic block, script field, or JSON location that caused the failure.
When applicable, provide a safer recommended rewrite or cleanup suggestion.

D1.Note / Feedback: If failed, specify the component label that caused the failure and provide a safer rewrite suggestion using fallback values, proper property access, or safe formatting.

D2.Note / Feedback: If failed, specify the component label, unsafe JavaScript or Form.io warning risk, why it may cause console errors or warnings, and a safer rewrite suggestion.

D3.Note / Feedback: If failed, specify the component label that caused the failure and the line number in JSON where console.log appears.

Traverse all components recursively, including nested child components inside panels, containers, columns, fieldsets, tabs, datagrids, editgrids, and other wrappers.

D1.review_item: Calculated value components must not show [Object], undefined,....
D1.description: Review whether calculated display-value components are protected from showing invalid or user-unfriendly output such as [object Object], undefined, null, NaN, or broken concatenated strings.
D1.goal: Make sure calculated display values are safely formatted and do not expose raw objects, missing values, null values, undefined values, NaN, or broken text to users.

output_style.feedback_requirement: If failed, specify the label of the component that caused the failure and provide a safer rewrite suggestion using fallback values, proper property access, or safe formatting.

example.Note / Feedback: Component label = "Employee Display Name" may display broken text because calculatedValue uses data.employee + ' - ' + data.department. If data.employee is an object, the output may become "[object Object] - Sales". If data.department is missing, the output may become "[object Object] - undefined". Safer rewrite: value = `${data.employee?.name || ''}${data.department ? ' - ' + data.department : ''}`.trim();

procedure:
Read the input Form.io JSON file from 
[numbered_source]
 to 
[/numbered_source].
Traverse all components recursively.
Inspect all components that contain display-value logic.
Prioritize components with calculatedValue, calculateValue, customDefaultValue, logic actions that set value, and similar calculated display expressions if present.
For each calculated display expression, check whether the output may produce invalid or user-unfriendly display text.
Detect risky outputs such as [object Object], undefined, null, NaN, broken concatenated strings such as "John undefined", "null - Sales", "undefined - undefined", or similar malformed display values.
Treat direct object concatenation into strings as risky.
Treat implicit object-to-string conversion as risky.
Treat use of fields that may be empty, null, or undefined without fallback values as risky.
Treat arithmetic expressions as risky if they may produce NaN due to missing, non-numeric, null, or undefined values.
Treat text concatenation without missing-value handling as risky.
Check whether the expression uses safe property access when reading object fields.
Check whether the expression uses fallback values such as || '', ?? '', default labels, Number(... ) with validation, Array.isArray checks, optional chaining, or explicit null/undefined checks.

Check whether object values are converted intentionally using a meaningful property such as name, label, value, code, id, or another business-relevant field instead of relying on implicit string conversion.
Mark this check as PASSED only if all calculated display values are protected against invalid output.
Mark this check as FAILED if any calculated display value may display [object Object], undefined, null, NaN, or similarly broken output text.

D2.review_item: Console must not show any JS error (or FormIO warning because FormIO will catch error and show as warning in console)
D2.description: Review whether executable JavaScript logic is protected from runtime errors or Form.io console warnings.
D2.goal: Make sure Form.io logic does not produce JavaScript runtime errors or Form.io warnings in the browser console.

output_style.feedback_requirement: If failed, specify the component label, the risky JavaScript or Form.io warning source, why it may show a console error or warning, and a safer rewrite suggestion.

example.Note / Feedback: Component label = "Customer Email" uses calculateValue with data.customer.email.trim(). This may cause a console warning or JavaScript error when data.customer or data.customer.email is undefined. Safer rewrite: value = (data.customer?.email || '').trim();

procedure:
Read the input Form.io JSON file from 
[numbered_source]
 to 
[/numbered_source].
Traverse the full Form.io JSON recursively.
Inspect all places that may contain JavaScript or executable logic.

Include but do not limit inspection to calculateValue, calculatedValue, customDefaultValue, customConditional, conditional expressions, validate.custom, logic blocks, trigger.javascript, action.javascript, and any nested script fields.
Check whether any JavaScript expression may throw a runtime error during form rendering, value calculation, validation, condition evaluation, or logic execution.
Detect risky nested property access without parent checks, such as data.a.b.c, row.a.b, input.value.name, or component.custom.x.y.

Detect method calls on values that may be null or undefined, such as .trim(), .map(), .filter(), .forEach(), .toLowerCase(), .toUpperCase(), .split(), .replace(), .includes(), .length, or date and numeric methods.
Detect unsafe array operations without Array.isArray checks when the source may not be an array.
Detect unsafe JSON.parse usage without try/catch or input validation.
Detect arithmetic or date operations that may produce NaN or Invalid Date without fallback handling.
Detect references to dependency fields that may not exist at the time the logic runs.
Detect syntax patterns that are likely to be incomplete, malformed, or incompatible with the Form.io execution context.
Treat Form.io warnings caused by caught JavaScript errors as failures, because Form.io may catch runtime errors and display them as warnings in the browser console.
Accept safe patterns such as optional chaining, nullish coalescing, fallback values, explicit if checks, typeof checks, Array.isArray checks, try/catch for risky parsing, and guarded method calls.
Mark this check as PASSED only if all inspected executable logic is unlikely to produce JavaScript errors or Form.io warnings in the console.
Mark this check as FAILED if any logic block may produce a JavaScript runtime error or Form.io warning.

D3.review_item: Console must not show debug logs.
D3.description: Review whether Form.io executable logic contains forbidden debug logging statements.
D3.goal: Make sure production Form.io JSON does not contain console.log debug statements, except inside the component labeled "ADMIN_Sys Attachment Auth".

output_style.feedback_requirement: If failed, specify the label of the component that caused the failure and the line number in JSON where console.log appears.

example.Note / Feedback: Component label = "Approval Decision" contains console.log at JSON line 428. Debug logs must be removed from Form.io logic before deployment.

Read the input Form.io JSON file from 
[numbered_source]
 to

Traverse the full Form.io JSON recursively.
Inspect all places that may contain JavaScript or executable logic.

Include but do not limit inspection to logic blocks, trigger.javascript, action.javascript, calculateValue, calculatedValue, customDefaultValue, customConditional, validate.custom, and nested script fields.
Check whether any debug logging statement using console.log exists.
If console.log appears inside a component whose label is exactly "ADMIN_Sys Attachment Auth", do not mark it as failed for this check.
If console.log appears outside the component whose label is exactly "ADMIN_Sys Attachment Auth", mark this check as FAILED.
When failing, report the component label and the line number in the JSON where console.log appears.
If the same component contains multiple console.log statements, report all relevant line numbers or the first line number with a note that multiple debug logs exist.
Mark this check as PASSED only if no forbidden console.log statement is found in any Form.io logic or script.
Mark this check as FAILED if any forbidden console.log statement is found.
